texts: mixed: the atoms are individually right, but the definite singular "The … harvest" makes the translator mint ONE particular harvest and say that occasion was a large collective ritual, instead of recording the recurring ritual as a kind — which is what a standing lore rule needs. Use a bare plural so the claim lands on the kind: "Salt-bloom new-moon harvests are large collective rituals."

bad: the three-part time frame comes apart into unrelated tags — "night", "new moon" and "salt-bloom season" sit side by side with the "night OF the new moon" link lost — and "new moon" is additionally taken apart as if it were a kind of object, asserting that a new moon is a moon and is "new", which the sentence does not claim. Name the occasion so it is stored as one opaque time symbol: "On Newmoon Night in salt-bloom season, a harvest party walks to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools." The rest of the clause is already right — the indefinite party stays a specific party, no tense is invented, and the tide-pools are the destination.
good. the collective subject takes a plain event with no spurious per-member rule, and "waxed coats" comes out as a coat kind with the treatment kept as a predicable modifier.
good. same clean shape as the coats sentence — "copper" stays inside the compound as a material noun, and the collective subject rightly gets no distribution rule.
good. "lasts until dawn" is recorded as an end point on the harvest itself rather than as a separate lasting event, which is the right shape for an event noun.

good. "Cauldron Hall" stays a named entity linked to the store by a loose association rather than an invented containment, and the pouring carries its content and destination with no invented result state.
